question: Six rounds of operator families have emitted nothing on this corpus. Is that a BUDGET problem (the right edit exists but is not reached) or a VOCABULARY problem (the right edit is not the kind of thing the family can express)?
answer: VOCABULARY, and now it is bounded rather than argued. Measured ceilings: 0/28 for a single substitutable edit, 1/28 for any number of substitutable edits, 0/28 an achieved solve.

traceback_frame.reading: A traceback-driven generator can only fire where the traceback names a source line. On the tasks that expose none, every operator family in this project has NO INPUT, so adding another form cannot raise the rate -- and that, not the vocabulary, is what the six families have been measuring all along.

the_generation_attempt.note: 920 candidates across 28 tasks. The zero is a measured zero, not a silent failure to run.

addition_shapes.reading: A shape that already occurs in the file is a template the repo supplies; a shape that does not is text no recombination of the file can produce. This decides whether an addition generator is worth building at all.

the_honest_reading: The traceback channel fires on 4 of 28 tasks (14%), because 24 of 28 fail on an assert raised inside the test file and expose no source line at all. Every traceback-keyed family in this project has NO INPUT on 86% of the corpus, which is what six rounds of 'zero emission' have actually been recording.
The assertion channel is empty: on those 24 tasks the expected value appears in the source once and lands near a fix line zero times. Printing expected-vs-actual to a generator supplies nothing.

The coverage channel is real and is the only one that works: running the failing test narrows 21,288 lines to 2,847 (86.6% reduction) and touches a fix line on 25 of 28 tasks. This is the first usable pointer this project has had to a line on the no-frame majority.

But pointing at the right line is not the wall. Of 667 changed sites, 498 never execute under the failing test, 144 are inexpressible as a substitution, and 25 are substitutable. Exactly 0 tasks have a single changed line that is a substitution on a covered line. The ceiling for the whole substitution family on this corpus is 1 of 28, and for a single-edit version of it 0 of 28.
The generation run achieved 0 of 28 against that 0-of-28 single-edit ceiling and a 1-of-28 multi-edit ceiling. It did not underperform; it was measured against a bound and matched it.

The fixes are ADDITIONS, not substitutions: 482 of 667 sites add statements, and 194 of 600 added statements have a shape that already occurs in the same file. An addition generator could in principle recombine templates the repo supplies, which is a different claim and is not tested here.
defects_found_in_my_own_instruments: import_roots put src/packaging on PYTHONPATH instead of src, making packaging a namespace package; the known-positive test then PASSED on the parent commit and 22 of 28 tasks were misreported NOT_FAIL_TO_PASS. Caught only because a task I had already solved appeared in that list.
the coverage plugin dumped from atexit after os was torn down and wrote an empty file, which is indistinguishable from 'the test executed nothing'. Eight rows carried a plausible 0.0 budget.
the coverage harness restored the parent commit, discarding the applied test file, and then ran a node that no longer existed.

the coverage plugin discarded import-time hits, deleting the module-level regex tables where one real fix in this corpus lives. Retention rose 0.159 -> 0.238 and task reach 22 -> 25 once import lines were kept.
failure_class let raw `assert a == b` expressions through as if they were exception names.
the first site classifier counted a two-line coordinated fix as a single edit because it iterated per file rather than per task shape; the single-edit ceiling is reported separately as a result.
what_this_is_not: Not a capability gain and not a benchmark row. 0 of 28 solves. The corpus is development data: every number here is measured on the same 28 tasks the project has been mining, so it can bound the generator but cannot demonstrate generalization.
